blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: On a film set, the camera move is committed during a take. Generative video reshooting lets filmmakers change it afterward, but may require hallucinating unrecorded content, a gap sometimes discovered only after leaving the set. We present Hybrid Cinematography, a workflow that bridges physical capture and generative reshooting to manage hallucination risk while filmmakers can still act on it. Using an editable 3D shot plan and a proxy of the take, our previsualization evaluates hallucination risk in real time. Seeing where the take lacks support, filmmakers can iteratively adjust the plan, explore moves that balance capture and generation, shoot guided pickups, or knowingly accept hallucination. We demonstrate the workflow through a mobile augmented reality application for on-set planning, capture, and review, and an offline pipeline for existing video. A study with experienced filmmakers reveals how previsualizing risk informs camera decisions and exposes tensions between creative intent and generative hallucination.
blocks.zh: 在电影集中,摄像头动作是在拍摄时进行的. 基因视频重拍让电影制作人事后改变,但可能要求幻觉未录制的内容,这个漏洞有时只在离开剧集后才发现. 我们介绍的是混合电影摄影, 这个工作流程连接 物理捕捉和基因重拍 来管理幻觉风险 而制片人仍然可以采取行动。 利用可编辑的3D镜头计划以及镜头的代名词,我们的预视性实时评估幻觉风险. 看到摄像头缺乏支持的地方,电影制作人可以迭代调整计划,探索平衡捕捉和生成的动作,拍摄引导的皮卡,或者在知情的情况下接受幻觉. 我们通过一个可移动的扩大现实应用软件来展示工作流程,用于设定规划、捕获和审查,以及用于现有视频的离线管道。 与经验丰富的电影制片人进行的一项研究揭示了预视风险如何为相机决策提供依据,并暴露了创作意图和基因幻觉之间的紧张关系.

blocks.en: Figure 1 . We present Hybrid Cinematography, a workflow connecting capture and generative post-production, built around one editable 3D shot plan that every stage reads (left). We demonstrate the workflow in a mobile augmented reality (AR) app. (a) Before or after capture, filmmakers plan the target move as keyframes by walking the scene, then set its timing. (b) In capture, the same plan drives the AR guidance. (c) In review, a previsualization (previs) checks the recorded take against that plan and marks what the model would have to invent, its hallucination risk . Every move between the captured move and the target move is a possible reshoot, asking the model to invent what the take does not support. Filmmakers navigate that range with a slider and see the risk of each move before anything is generated (right). They can then revise the move, capture more, re-time, or knowingly accept hallucination, while still on set. Video and examples: https://hybridcinematography.github.io/ Two-part figure. The left part, titled The Hybrid Cinematography Workflow, shows three stages connected in a loop around one 3D shot plan. In (a) Shot planning, people walk a scene and place camera keyframes in AR, joined by a dashed blue path. In (b) AR-guided capture, a person with a phone follows a trail of chevrons when far from a keyframe and matches its pose when near. In (c) Review and refine, a person holds a tablet that shows the previs and a slider. Two cards below the tablet compare the captured handheld path with the planned target path and show a slider that interpolates between them. A blue arrow labeled revise the same path and timing leads from review back to planning, and a dashed teal loop labeled guided additional capture leads from review back to capture. The right part, titled Previsualize hallucination risk before generating, enlarges the tablet screen. Three previs images sit at slider positions 0.00 (captured, lower risk), 0.67 (intermediate, balances capture and generation), and 1.00 (target, higher risk). Red hatching marks missing coverage and a blue-to-yellow heatmap marks resolution and performance deficits. Both grow from the captured end toward the target end. A card under each image shows the matching camera path and slider position. Four responses sit along the bottom: revise the move, capture more, re-time, and accept hallucination.

blocks.en: 1. Introduction
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 导言

blocks.en: Previsualization and planning tools have long played a critical role in creative domains that benefit from extensive amounts of attention to detail. Whether it is armature sketching for illustration, storyboarding or animatics for film, or wireframe renders for CGI, the goal is the same, to revise decisions before production becomes expensive. In filmmaking, that flexibility traditionally ends when the camera rolls. Executing a complex camera move, such as an orbit, crane, or push-in, requires meticulous choreography, specialized equipment, or skilled operators. Once a take is filmed, altering the camera move traditionally requires another take.
blocks.zh: 视觉和规划工具长期以来在从大量关注细节中受益的创造性领域发挥了关键作用。 无论是为插图、故事板画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画画, 在电影制作中,这种灵活性传统上会随着相机的滚动而结束. 执行复杂的相机移动,例如轨道、起重机或推入,需要精密的舞蹈、专门设备或熟练的操作人员。 一旦拍摄了镜头,改变相机动作传统上需要再拍摄一次.

blocks.en:
Generative video reshooting changes this.
Given a recorded take, these models can render the same performance from a new camera trajectory chosen or revised after capture ( Bai et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ; Lin et al., 2026 ) .
However, a target trajectory may require rendering things that were not visible at all, or not visible in sufficient detail, in the captured trajectory, leaving parts of the shot for the model to hallucinate. We call this unrecorded demand the shot’s hallucination risk . A direct response is to capture additional takes covering alternative camera moves. Yet doing so consumes scarce production time and cannot reproduce the exact moment of a live performance. Moreover, filmmakers may discover that a different move is needed only when editing against adjacent footage. Generative reshooting offers another response: infer the missing content from the recorded take. Research in this area has focused on improving that inference through advances in generative modeling and more extensive use of recorded footage. These improvements, however, do not by themselves help filmmakers decide what additional footage to capture or what content they are willing to let the model hallucinate.
On one extreme we have the challenges of cinematography, and on the other extreme we have the risks of hallucination.
Navigating that spectrum is going to define a lot of cinematography in the future.
blocks.zh:
基因视频重拍改变了这一点。
根据记录的拍摄结果,这些模型可以从捕获后选择或修改的新相机轨迹中得出相同的性能(Bai等,2025;Zhang等,2025;Lin等,2026)。
然而,目标轨迹可能需要在被捕获的轨迹中渲染出完全不可见或不够详细可见的东西,让部分镜头让模型产生幻觉. 我们称这为没有记录的要求, 一个直接的对策是捕捉更多覆盖其他相机动作的镜头. 然而这样做会消耗有限的生产时间,无法复制现场表演的确切时刻。 此外,电影制片人可能发现,只有在根据相邻镜头进行编辑时,才需要采取不同的动作. generative reshooting提供了另一个回应:从所记录的取材中推断出缺失的内容. 这一领域的研究侧重于通过在基因模型制作和更广泛地使用所记录的镜头方面取得进展来改进这种推论。 然而,这些改进本身并不能帮助电影制作人决定要拍摄哪些额外镜头,或者他们愿意让模型产生幻觉的内容.
一方面,我们面临电影拍摄的挑战,另一方面,我们面临幻觉的风险。
导航这个光谱 将会在未来定义很多电影。

blocks.en: In this work, we present Hybrid Cinematography, a workflow that connects physical camera capture and generative reshooting around an editable 3D shot plan. While the plan specifies the camera move the filmmaker wants, a lightweight 3D proxy represents what the take recorded. Evaluating views along a camera move against this proxy produces a previsualization (previs) of hallucination risk that updates in real time as filmmakers revise the move. This lets filmmakers rapidly explore moves between the captured and target trajectories, inspecting trade-offs between physical capture and hallucination without waiting for the generative model.
blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们呈现了混合相机(Hybrid Cinematography),一种连接物理相机捕捉和基因重拍的工作流程,围绕可编辑的3D拍摄计划. 虽然计划指定了电影制作人想要的相机移动,但一个轻量级的3D代理代表了拍摄记录的内容. 透过相机移动来评价观点, 这让电影制片人能快速地探索被捕获与目标轨迹之间的移动,在不等待基因模型的情况下检查物理捕获与幻觉之间的取舍.

blocks.en: We demonstrate this workflow both on set and during editing. On set, a mobile augmented reality (AR) application brings the previsualization into shot planning, guided capture, and review, letting filmmakers revise the move or capture additional footage while the physical scene is still available (Figure 1 ). During editing, an offline pipeline applies the same previsualization to existing video, letting filmmakers explore alternative camera moves and decide what hallucination they are willing to accept before committing to generation (Figure 7 ).
blocks.zh: 我们在集中和编辑时都演示这个工作流程. 在设定时,一个移动增强现实(AR)应用程序将预视化引入了镜头规划,引导捕捉和审查,让电影制片人在物理场景仍然可用时修改动作或捕捉到更多镜头(图一. 在编辑期间,一个离线管道对现有视频采用同样的预视,让电影制作人探索另类相机动作,并决定在承诺生成之前他们愿意接受何种幻觉(图7).

blocks.en: We evaluated Hybrid Cinematography in a two-part study with seven experienced filmmakers across cinematography, directing, and video production. Participants used the previs to revise camera moves and choose targeted capture responses, reporting less pressure to execute a perfect take on set. Their decisions revealed tensions between reducing hallucination risk and preserving creative intent, as well as between accepting plausible generated content and maintaining the authenticity of the recorded take.
blocks.zh: 我们通过一个分为两部分的研究评估了混合电影学,有七位有经验的电影制片人参与了电影学、导演和录像制作。 与会者利用预告片修改相机动作并选择有针对性的捕捉反应,报告执行完美摄取相机的压力较小. 他们的决定显示,在减少幻觉风险和保持创造性意图之间,以及在接受可信生成的内容和保持所记录的摄取的真实性之间,存在着矛盾。

blocks.en: Our contributions include: • Hybrid Cinematography , a workflow for navigating trade-offs along the continuum between captured and target camera moves, balancing physical capture against generative hallucination (Section 3 ). • Strategies for visualizing hallucination risk that expose where and why a recorded take lacks support for a target camera move, pairing distinct deficits with targeted responses before generation (Section 4 ). • A prototype mobile AR application and an offline pipeline that demonstrate this workflow across on-set capture and post-production editing (Section 5 ). • Findings from a study with seven experienced filmmakers on how they use previsualized hallucination risk to make camera decisions and negotiate tensions between hallucination, creative intent, and the authenticity of recorded performance (Section 6 ).
blocks.zh: 我们的贡献包括: 混合电影摄影,这是沿着捕捉到的相机动作与目标相机动作之间的连续体进行权衡的工作流程,平衡物理捕捉与基因幻觉(第3节)。 · 视觉幻觉风险战略,这种风险暴露在有记录的摄入地点和原因,缺乏对目标相机移动的支持,将明显的缺陷与世代前的定向反应结合起来(第4节)。 • 与7名有经验的电影制片人进行的一项研究的结果,即他们如何利用预视的幻觉风险来作出相机决定并谈判幻觉、创造性意图和所记录的表演真实性之间的紧张关系(第6节)。

blocks.zh: 2. 相关工作

blocks.en:
Prior work in camera planning and video reshooting largely separates capture
from generation. Reshooting models treat the take as fixed and hallucinate whatever a
target move asks for that the take does not contain. Capture guidance and
previsualization, conversely, help filmmakers plan and execute camera moves
without anticipating computational synthesis. Neither tells a filmmaker, while
the scene is still standing, what a move would leave to the model.

blocks.en: 2.1. Generative Video Reshooting
blocks.zh: 2.1. 基因视频再拍摄

blocks.en:
Generative reshooting models re-render a recorded take from a new camera
trajectory, conditioning directly on the source video ( Bai et al., 2025 ) or anchoring generation to geometry rendered from the target
camera ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Ren et al., 2025 ; Yu et al., 2025 ; Paliwal et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026 ) .
Geometry-based pipelines pass a rendered proxy and a support mask to the
model. This proxy is typically a 3D point cloud or a time-varying 4D
representation, but the mask records only where it has holes. It does not
distinguish a surface that was never observed from one sampled too coarsely for
the requested framing, nor does it describe whether performance evidence is
valid at the requested time. Prior work treats synthesis across those gaps as a
capability: the ReCapture reshooting model ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) , for
example, reports that the model can plausibly hallucinate scene content outside
the source view. For a capture workflow, however, that capability is also an
unrecorded production decision: neither the mask nor the generated pixels tell
the filmmaker whether the hallucination was avoidable.

Recent work reduces unsupported generations by routing more of the take
into the result ( Paliwal et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026 ) , completing unseen
geometry with additional models ( Cao et al., 2026 ; Jin et al., 2026 ) ,

by a model that never saw it either. Vista4D ( Lin et al., 2026 ) , which we
adopt as our downstream reshooting model, can incorporate additional scene takes
to reduce hallucination, but it does not tell a filmmaker which observations a
particular reshoot requires. These methods make
increasingly sophisticated use of evidence, but only after capture. None of
them evaluate hallucination risk while a filmmaker can still record the missing
support.

blocks.en: 2.2. Shot Authoring and Previsualization
blocks.zh: 2.2. 拍摄写作和预视

blocks.en:
Previsualization lets filmmakers evaluate framing, camera movement, and
performance before committing production resources. In virtual cinematography,
early work automated camera placement and pacing by encoding film idioms as
procedural rules ( He et al., 1996 ) , while subsequent tools gave authors
interactive control over viewpoint selection through geometric
constraints ( Lino and Christie, 2015 ; Lino et al., 2011 ) . CollageVis brings recorded acting
into this process, arranging segmented performers as video layers on a virtual
stage ( Jo et al., 2024 ) . This preserves the performance without requiring
character animation, but showing the acting from another direction requires
another take. Generative reshooting offers a way to view a recorded performance
from new directions, but raises the opposite problem: asking for views the take
never recorded.

blocks.en:
PrevizWhiz uses rough 3D scenes and video references to guide generative
video previsualization ( Hu et al., 2026a ) , providing resemblance controls to
steer adherence to the authored scene and motion controls to adjust performance
detail. But PrevizWhiz begins from virtual designs and text prompts, where
hallucinated details are part of ideation. In a live-action take, hallucination
can compromise the authenticity of a recorded performance. Other systems
connect shot authoring directly to physical capture and subsequent editing
through shared representations. CineCraft uses a persistent storyboard-derived
shot plan to coordinate AR guidance, focus and zoom automation, and rough-cut
assembly ( Tran et al., 2026 ) . Hybrid Tours frames a spectrum between all-real and
all-virtual workflows, letting users pick a point on it by filtering and
combining short captured clips into longer camera
trajectories ( Liu et al., 2025 ) . We take that spectrum as an interaction target.
Where Hybrid Tours has users choose among clips they captured, we make the
range between the captured move and the target move continuously navigable
within a single take, attaching a real-time readout of the hallucination risk each stop
incurs. More broadly, while these systems carry one representation across
production stages, the take is always what a later stage consumes. It is never
what the plan is measured against. Our previs makes that measurement
visible as filmmakers change the camera path and its timing.

Mixed-initiative interfaces allow computational systems to assist without

than aesthetic appearance ( Amershi et al., 2019 ) . Generative reshooting
makes this unusually difficult: the output is a finished-looking video, and
nothing in it separates the parts that reproduce the take from the parts the
model hallucinated.

Today a filmmaker records a take, leaves the set, chooses a target move, generates, and inspects the result for what the model had to hallucinate. Hybrid Cinematography checks the take’s support for a move before generation, from a proxy of the take, which makes the check cheap enough to repeat and early enough to capture more:

blocks.en:
To evaluate these deficits without running the generative model, we construct a 3D proxy of the take consisting of an accumulated static point cloud and time-indexed performer point clouds (DG1).
Rendering this proxy along a move produces target-view point projections and binary support masks that match the conditioning representations required by downstream reshooting models such as Vista4D ( Lin et al., 2026 ) . The previs then tests the observations backing each rendered point against our three deficits in milliseconds, enabling instant feedback as filmmakers edit a move.

blocks.en: 5.2. Capturing With the Plan as Guidance
blocks.zh: 5.2. 将计划作为指导

blocks.en: During a take, the shot plan acts as virtual marks on the floor, guiding camera execution in 3D space (DG4, Figure 1 b). To prevent visual clutter during capture, the interface employs progressive disclosure (Figure 5 ). When the operator is far from the next keyframe, coarse guidance projects breadcrumb arrows on the ground indicating where to move. As the operator approaches, these arrows give way to fine guidance : the target camera’s frustum, distance readouts, and framing cues to settle the shot. Guidance applies equally to rehearsal walks and pickup tasks (Section 5.3 ).

blocks.en:
Importantly, guidance does not enforce rigid adherence. If the operator
departs from the planned path, the take is not discarded. Instead, review
evaluates whatever evidence the camera recorded. This allows operators to focus
on capturing the scene rather than chasing mechanical precision. During capture, the device records RGB video, hardware LiDAR depth, and ARKit 6-DoF camera poses, while tracking performers in real time using EdgeTAM ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) . These streams populate the static and dynamic stores of the proxy for immediate on-device review.

Review brings the target view, timeline, compromise slider, and 3D risk
map together on a single screen (DG1, DG2, Figure 6 ).
Tapping a flagged region opens an actionable response card tailored to that
deficit (DG3, Figure 6 E–F). Rather than prescribing an
automated fix, the interface supports three explicit production actions (DG5):

timing curve, or inspect two automated proposals. Reduce move pulls the slider back toward the captured move until the flagged region is supported. Retime searches for a camera velocity schedule that slows down where the take provides support and accelerates through unsupported spans, while preserving authored holds (Appendix D ). Proposals are visualized with their trade-offs and never applied automatically (DG5). • Capture more. For coverage or resolution deficits, tapping the card creates a targeted pickup task. The app freezes the unsupported region and time span and extracts one or two guidance viewpoints. The operator then captures a brief pickup take, which is folded into the proxy and immediately re-evaluated to verify that the gap has been closed. • Accept hallucination. When a missing region is deemed artistically inconsequential or easily synthesized (such as an unfeatured background wall), the filmmaker explicitly confirms it (DG5). The interface records an acceptance mask tied to the current shot plan. Any subsequent edit to the move or take clears the acceptance, ensuring that only deliberate decisions reach post-production.

From these inputs, it constructs the 3D proxy and serves it to a browser-based viewer with the same slider, timeline lanes, and diagnostic overlays (DG2). blocks.en: We evaluated the Hybrid Cinematography workflow with seven experienced filmmakers to examine how practitioners read hallucination risk and navigate production trade-offs. Because this approach introduces an unprecedented coupling between physical camera capture and generative reshooting, no direct baseline exists. Following prior evaluations of interactive creative tools without direct counterparts ( Hu et al., 2026a ; Tran et al., 2026 ; Jo et al., 2024 ; Suzuki et al., 2020 ; Leiva et al., 2020 ) , we report qualitative sessions examining how filmmakers reason about shot planning, guided capture, and hallucination risk across production and post-production.
blocks.zh: 我们与七位有经验的电影制作人一起评估了混合电影制片工作流程,以考察从业者如何读取幻觉风险并引导生产取舍。 由于这种方法引入了物理相机捕捉与基因再射之间前所未有的耦合,因此不存在直接基线. 在事先对没有直接对应方的互动创作工具进行评估(Hu等,2026a;Tran等,2026;Jo等,2024;铃木等,2020;Leiva等,2020;)之后,我们报告定性会议,审查电影制作人如何解释拍摄规划、指导性捕捉和整个生产和生产后的幻觉风险。

blocks.en: 6.2. Study Design
blocks.zh: 6.2. 研究设计

blocks.en: Part 1 introduces participants to hallucination risk in a browser viewer using an offline take before working on set. Participants first rate how comfortable they would be using a generative model to add a new camera move to their own recorded takes, providing the baseline for Figure 8 A. A tutorial sequence introduces the interactive slider and previs. An initial inspection task pairs a take filmed from the side with a front view synthesized by a reshooting model, asking participants to place pins where they believe the model had to invent content (Figure 9 a). A reveal then overlays the diagnostic map of what the camera never recorded, confirming their intuition by highlighting unobserved background surfaces in red and the performer’s face in yellow (Figure 9 b). The second scene moves participants into the previs reconstructed from the take, using an orbit around the performer as the target move (Figure 9 c). The slider lets them move between the captured move and target move to inspect support. After modifying the target move and exploring the previs, participants stop at an acceptable slider position and explain the trade-off. Finally, they rate their comfort a second time.
blocks.zh: 第一部分向参与者介绍浏览器使用离线取景器进行幻觉风险,然后进行设定. 与会者首先评估他们使用基因模型在自己记录的摄入量中添加新相机动作的舒适程度,为图8 A提供了基线。 一个教程序列引入了交互式幻灯片和预览. 初步检查任务配对从侧面拍摄出由再拍摄模型所合成的前视相片,要求参与者在他们认为模型必须发明内容的地方放出针(图9 a). 然后,一个透露内容覆盖了摄像机从未记录的诊断图,通过以红色突出未观察背景表面和以黄色突出表演者的脸(图9b)来证实其直觉。 第二个场景将参与者移动入从摄取中重建的预告片中,以一个围绕表演者的轨道作为目标移动(图9 c). 滑动器让他们在被捕获的移动与目标移动之间移动来检查支持. 在修改了目标移动并探索预告后,参与者会停留在可接受的滑动位置并解释取舍. 最后,他们再次评价他们的舒适感。

blocks.en: Part 2 moves participants onto the set, where our mobile application demonstrates the full workflow combining shot planning, guided capture, and review against the previs. Following a fifteen-minute tutorial, participants plan concatenated paths in augmented reality and customize timing along each. They capture three scenes, including one with a performer and one with a prop. For each take, the experimenter acts as director and requests a change after capture, such as speeding through one stretch and slowing through another. Participants refine the shot in the app, editing path and timing, and navigating between revising the move, retiming, capturing more, or accepting synthesis via the slider while thinking aloud throughout. Finally, they complete a questionnaire on planning, capture, review, and the workflow as a whole (Figure 8 C).
blocks.zh: 第二部分将参与者推到集中,我们的移动应用程序展示了将拍摄规划、引导捕获和审查与预告相结合的整个工作流程。 在15分钟的辅导之后,参与者计划采用强化现实的修饰路径,并按每个路径定制时间安排。 他们捕捉出三个场景,包括一个有表演者,一个有道具. 对于每次拍摄,实验者都担任导演并请求在被捕获后进行改变,例如超速通过一个拉伸并减速通过另一个拉伸. 参与者在应用中完善了镜头,编辑路径和时间,并在修改动作,刺激,捕捉更多,或者通过滑动器接受合成,同时在整个过程中高声思考. 最后,他们完成了关于规划、捕捉、审查和整个工作流程的调查问卷(图8 C)。

blocks.en: 6.3. Findings
blocks.zh: 6.3. 调查结果

blocks.en: We organize our findings around four themes that reflect the production workflow: (1) authoring and guided capture with a unified shot plan, (2) diagnosing hallucination risk and navigating trade-offs before generation, (3) selecting targeted responses for distinct deficits, and (4) how filmmaker comfort grew with active agency and control.
blocks.zh: 我们围绕反映生产工作流程的四个主题组织我们的调查结果:(1) 以统一的拍摄计划编写和引导抓取,(2) 诊断幻觉风险和在一代人之前的取舍,(3) 选择针对明显缺陷的定向对策,(4) 电影制作人安心如何随着积极的代理和控制而成长.

blocks.en: 6.3.1. Carrying a Unified Shot Plan from Preproduction Through Capture
blocks.zh: 6.3.1. 通过捕捉实施统一射击计划

blocks.en: Planning a camera path with AR keyframes was rated easy, with a median of 7 of 7 (Figure 8 C). P4 observed that walking keyframes felt “directly transferable” to how a DP plans a scene by placing the camera where a move starts and ends. On set, guidance replaced marks on the floor (P5), was more precise than a verbal walkthrough (P1), and made physically difficult moves feasible (P2).
blocks.zh: 用AR键帧规划相机路径被评为易取,中位数为7分(图8 C). P4观察到行走的键框感觉“可直接转移”到DP如何规划场景,将相机放入动作开始和结束的地方。 在套装上,取而代之的指针在地上(P5)比走口(P1)更精确,使实际操作困难可行(P2)。

blocks.en: Different production backgrounds shaped distinct mental models for camera planning. While cinematographers like P4 anchored planning to physical marks on set, P3 (who brought a 3D animation background, rating guidance 4 of 7) expected keyframes to follow 3D timeline conventions, noting that guidance meant she would “only need to capture key frames instead of get the precise movement.” Beyond individual operation, unifying authoring and capture into an editable plan (DG4) provided a shared reference for crew communication (P1, P2, P6). P1 described the AR path as “almost like a 3D storyboard” that makes it “much easier to convey the vision and timing for a shot across a small-production crew,” replacing verbal walkthroughs (P6) and helping crews get on board with complex moves (P2).
blocks.zh: 不同的生产背景为相机规划塑造了独特的精神模型. 虽然P4等电影制片人将规划定位到设定的物理标记,但P3(他们带来了3D动画背景,评分指导为7分之4)期望关键框架遵循3D时间表常规,指出指导意味着她将“只需要捕捉关键框架,而不是获得精确的运动”。 除了个人操作外,将作者和捕获统一为可编辑计划(DG4),为机组通信(P1,P2,P6)提供了共享的参考. P1将AR路径描述为"几乎像一款3D故事板",这使得它"非常容易传达出拍摄镜头的视觉和时间跨出一个小型制作的机组","取代了口语走行道(P6)并用复杂的动作帮助机组人员登机(P2).

blocks.en: Having pickups available changed how participants shot takes. Relieved of single-take pressure, operators felt freer moving the camera (P2) and, as P5 put it, “more free to make mistakes,” because the workflow “allows for preplanning to occur without too much pressure for the actual moment.” Operators prioritized live performance over background coverage (P2), used the visual path to rehearse marks (P3), and noted its value for unrepeatable documentary moments (P5).
blocks.zh: 可用接头改变了参与者射击的方式。 因为工作流程“预谋在实际时间不会造成太多的压力”。 操作员将现场表演置于背景覆盖之上(P2),利用视觉路径来排练标记(P3),并指出其对无法重现的记录片刻(P5)的价值。

blocks.en: 6.3.2. Reading Hallucination Risk and Navigating Trade-offs Before Generation
blocks.zh: 6.3.2. 读取 " 幻觉 " 风险和 " 世代取舍 "

blocks.en: Previsualizing hallucination risk before generation (DG1) made model dependencies immediately interpretable. All participants correctly identified the hallucinated face in the initial inspection task before overlays were explained, and rated the previs a median of 7 of 7 for showing where and why the model must invent content (Figure 8 C). Participants valued knowing on set what the footage supported (P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7). P2 was “immediately aware what the tools in post will and will not hallucinate,” while P3 appreciated knowing “what needs to be AI-generated instead of burning tokens and leave it up to fate.”
blocks.zh: 在产生前可视化出幻觉风险(DG1),使得模型依赖性可以立即被解释. 所有参与者在解释重叠之前正确识别出初始检查任务中的幻相相,并将预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预预 与会者重视了解录像所支持的内容(P2、P3、P4、P5、P6、P7)。 P2“立即意识到后台中的工具将会产生什么,不会产生什么幻觉”,而P3则赞赏知道“什么需要由AI生成,而不是烧掉活物,留给命运。 “

blocks.en: Participants rated the previs and slider a median of 6 of 7 for exploring acceptable trade-offs (DG2). When navigating between the captured move and target move, stopping points reflected qualitative judgments about scene content rather than a numerical threshold (Figure 8 B). Participants stopped where performer identity or facial fidelity degraded (P2, P3), where the intended move survived with the actor at low risk (P6), or where, as P5 cautioned, “you might as well have AI make the whole movie.”
blocks.zh: 与会者将预告和滑盘评为7分之6,以探索可接受的取舍(DG2)。 在被捕获移动与目标移动之间进行导航时,截取点反映了对场景内容的定性判断,而不是一个数值阈值(图8 B). 与会者停止了表演者身份或面部忠诚程度下降(P2,P3)的地方,停止了打算与低风险演员(P6)一起生存的动作,停止了如P5所警告的“你可能不如让AI拍摄整部电影。 “

blocks.en: Rather than passively accepting generation costs, participants actively reshaped the input by revising the target move (DG4, P5, P6, P7). Both modifying keyframes and adjusting the slider to alter model conditioning, updating the previs interactively. Session logs revealed participants iteratively alternating between both controls: adjusting keyframes, sweeping the slider to inspect updated support, and refining the path again. P7 edited keyframes 25 times to “limit the visibility of generated wall at the end,” and P6 made 20 adjustments until the path retained “the effect I wanted to achieve and there is less hallucination occurred.”
blocks.zh: 参与者不是被动地接受生成成本,而是通过修订目标移动(DG4,P5,P6,P7)来积极重塑投入. 既修改了键框,又调整了滑动器来改变模型条件,交互地更新了预览. 会话日志显示参与者在两个控件之间迭代交替交替:调整密钥框,将滑动器扫地检查更新后的支持,并再次改进路径. P7编辑了25次键框,以“在结尾限制所生成的墙的能见度”,P6作了20次调整,直到路径保留了“我想达到的效果,发生幻觉较少。 “

blocks.en: 6.3.3. Selecting Targeted Responses for Distinct Deficits
blocks.zh: 6.3.3. 选择针对不同缺陷的针对性对策

blocks.en: Selecting a highlighted deficit in the previs opens a response card with tailored remedy actions (DG3, DG5), letting participants preview solutions before deciding how to respond. For static background gaps, participants could launch a guided pickup or pull back the slider. For unobserved performer angles, where static pickups cannot recover live action, the interface offered retiming proposals, path edits, or replacement takes. With capture available on set in Part 2, participants prioritized filming targeted pickups for static deficits over exhausting the crew on repeated full takes (P1, P2, P3, P4, P6). P3 noted that getting “pickup shots just for missing info instead of trying to do one perfect shot over and over again” helps most with “budgeting and choose the important shots to keep.” P5 valued knowing “what wiggle room we’d have on a shot” on tight schedules, and P6 noted that deciding on set “is better than regretting a decision later on when discovering a problem in editing.” Ratings for whether on-set warnings helped decide between a pickup, a retake, and synthesis yielded a median of 6 of 7.
blocks.zh: 选择预告中突出的缺陷会打开一个带有特制补救动作的响应卡(DG3,DG5),让参与者在决定如何回应之前预览解决方案. 对于静态背景空白,参与者可以推出有引导的接车或拉回滑行器. 对于无法观察的表演者角度,当静态接取器无法恢复活动作时,接口会提供再刺激建议,路径编辑,或替换取用. 根据第二编的设定,与会者优先拍摄静态不足的定点皮卡,而不是重复全收的机组人员疲劳(P1、P2、P3、P4、P6)。 P3指出,“只为丢失的信息取出枪口,而不是一次又一次地尝试完美地取出枪口”对“编制预算和选择保留的重要枪口”帮助最大。 P5很重视在紧凑的日程上知道“我们拍到什么动静的房间 ” , P6指出,“在编辑中发现一个问题时,决定一个动静“总比稍后决定后悔好。 对设定的警告是否有助于在接车、重拍和合成之间作出决定的评级得出7分之6的中位数。

blocks.en: When addressing performance deficits or director requests to alter pacing, participants explored both interactive timing adjustments and automated proposals. Decoupling camera pacing from the spatial path made tuning timing easy (median 6 of 7, with P4, P5, and P6 rating 7 of 7). P6 observed that “with the timing tool I don’t need to follow the plan exactly and still achieve the timing effect I want.” When evaluating automated retiming proposals that linger in supported views and accelerate through unobserved angles (Appendix D ), participants appreciated the proposal as a structural reference, but exercised caution in dynamic scenes. Retiming modifies only camera progress along its path while the recorded performer continues at natural speed on an unchanged clock. Even so, because camera speed guides emotional rhythm and audience attention, automated accelerations risked clashing with the performer’s dramatic beats (P4, P5). As P4 noted, for a scene “where an actor is performing because the performance changes every time,” preserving dramatic intent took precedence over automated schedules. Participants therefore preferred manually sculpting camera timing, shortening the move spatially via keyframes and the compromise slider, or filming an intentional retake.
blocks.zh: 在处理业绩不足或主任要求改变进度时,与会者探讨了互动时间安排调整和自动化建议。 与空间路径脱钩相机相距使调制定时变得容易(中间为7分6分,其中P4分5分,P6分7分. P6评论道,“用计时工具,我并不需要完全按照计划行事,而是需要达到我想要的计时效果。” 在评价那些停留在支持的观点中并通过无人观察角度加速的建议(附录D)时,与会者赞赏该建议作为结构性参考,但在动态场景中谨慎行事。 重新定时只改变相机沿着其路径前进,而录制的表演者则以自然速度在不变的时钟上继续. 即便如此,由于相机速度引导了情感节奏和观众注意力,自动加速也有可能与表演者的戏剧性节拍相冲突(P4,P5). 正如P4所指出的,对于一个“演员表演是因为表演每次都有变化”的场景,保持戏剧性的意图优先于自动时间表。 因此,与会者倾向于手动雕刻相机时间,通过键框和折中滑板缩短移动空间,或者拍摄有意重拍.

blocks.en: No participant was willing to delegate the performer to the model in either Part 1 or Part 2. Across all seven participants, facial fidelity marked the strict boundary where slider exploration stopped. P4 insisted that “nothing to be hallucinated on the face,” P7 remained cautious about generating human faces consistently, and P5 emphasized that synthetic infill compromises authentic performance, noting that “false emotions, and dialogue also would leave me uncomfortable.”
blocks.zh: 没有任何与会者愿意将表演者委托到第1部分或第2部分的模式。 在所有7名参与者中,面部忠贞是停止滑道探测的严格边界。 P4坚持认为,“脸上没有任何幻觉”,P7对不断产生人相持谨慎态度,P5强调,合成填充会损害真正的表现,指出“虚假的情绪和对话也会使我感到不舒服。 “

blocks.en: Beyond faces and performance, participants drew boundaries wherever the production had invested creative effort. These included key props (P6), dressed sets (P2), critical story beats (P4), and on-screen text (P3, P6). These decisions reflected narrative importance rather than pixel area. As P1 observed, “the amount of infill is less concerning than the quality of the regions that need infill.” Deciding what to leave to the model was recognized as a shared crew decision, with P5 likening real-time diagnostic checks to “the existence of the script supervisor” when agreeing on boundaries with the director.
blocks.zh: 除了面相和表现之外,与会者在生产投入创造性努力的地方划定界限。 其中包括关键道具(P6),外装套装(P2),批判故事节拍(P4)和屏幕上文字(P3,P6). 这些决定反映了叙述性的重要性,而不是像素领域。 正如P1所指出,“填充量与需要填充的区域的质量相比较少。” 确定留给模型什么被确认为共同的乘务员决定,P5在与导演商定界限时将实时诊断检查比作“脚本主管的存在”。

blocks.en: 6.3.4. Filmmaker Comfort Grew with Active Agency and Control
blocks.zh: 6.3.4. 电影制片人与积极机构和控制

blocks.en: Evaluating whether footage is sufficient to move on is an essential step on set. Confidence to wrap a scene knowing how well the take supported the target shot received a median rating of 6 of 7 (Figure 8 C). P1 gave a more conservative rating (3 of 7), noting that on-set wrap confidence assumes the target path is already known: “The biggest hurdle is it relies on knowing some aspects of re-shooting while shooting. If I knew what the desired paths would be, I would have used those to begin with.” When camera moves are chosen during editing rather than planned on set, P1 valued the feedback for understanding scene limitations during post-production handoffs rather than declaring a scene wrapped.
blocks.zh: 评估镜头是否足以继续拍摄,是设定上必不可少的一步。 自信地将场景包裹起来,知道拍摄的拍摄支持程度有多好,获得中位数为6分7分(图8 C). P1给出了更保守的评分(3分为7分),指出设定的包装自信假设目标路径已经知道: “最大的障碍是它依赖了解射击时重新射击的某些方面。 如果我知道所希望的道路是什么,我就会用这些道路开始。” 当在编辑过程中选择相机动作而不是在设定上进行规划时,P1重视反馈,在制作后交接时理解场景限制,而不是宣布一个场景被包裹.

blocks.en: Across the entire workflow, filmmaker comfort with generative reshooting increased for all participants (Figure 8 A), rising from a median of 4 before the study to 6 after experiencing the on-set system. Participants attributed this increase to a sense of agency and transparency rather than uncritical trust in generative models (P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7). P5 shifted from viewing generative tools as “unfaithful to my profession” to concluding that “now it feels like a helper.” P6’s comfort grew even as he became “more cautious about AI generated shots,” because diagnostic feedback allowed him to actively prevent hallucinations “by controlling my shot angles.” Three participants anticipated attempting camera moves they would not have risked before (P1, P2, P7). P7 explained that previsualizing support provides the evidence needed to secure “buy-in from DP and their department,” enabling crews to plan “unusual, ambitious shots and maximizing the likelihood of a positive outcome.”
blocks.zh: 在整个工作流程中,所有参与者的电影制片人对基因重拍的舒适度都有所提高(图8 A),在经历了固定系统后,从研究前的中位数4上升到了6. 与会者将这种增加归因于一种代理意识和透明度,而不是对基因模型(P2,P3,P4,P5,P6,P7)的不批判性信任. P5从将基因工具视为“不忠于我的职业”转向得出结论“现在感觉自己像个帮手 ” 。 P6的舒适感在“对AI更谨慎地产生出镜头”时增加, 3名与会者预计,他们以前不会冒险尝试相机移动(P1、P2、P7)。 P7解释说,预视支助提供了必要的证据,以确保“从DP及其部门购买”,使机组人员能够规划“不寻常、雄心勃勃的镜头并尽可能地取得积极成果。 “

blocks.en: 7. Discussion
blocks.zh: 7. 联合国 讨论情况

blocks.en: We reflect on how previsualizing hallucination risk can change how filmmakers work with generative models, and discuss several design tensions and considerations for generative tools that reach beyond filmmaking.
blocks.zh: 我们思考先入为主的幻觉风险如何改变电影人如何与基因模型合作,并讨论超越电影制作的基因工具在设计上的紧张和考虑。

blocks.en: 7.1. Seeing Hallucination Risk Changes How Filmmakers Shoot
blocks.zh: 7.1. 见幻觉风险如何改变电影制作者的拍摄方式

blocks.en: Filmmaking is an iterative loop: crews plan a shot, rehearse it, roll a take, and repeat until the result is good enough to move on. Moving on is a production call that balances creative goals against time and budget. Under tight schedules, crews often move on and rely on post-production to salvage unresolved defects (P3, P5). Generative reshooting expands what post-production can fix, and with it, what a crew might be willing to leave uncaptured. Yet what the model will actually have to invent remains unknown until the set is struck and it is too late to capture more. The previs brings that check directly into the production loop, before the call to move on.
blocks.zh: 电影制作是一个迭代循环:剧组计划出一出镜头,进行排练,滚动一出,并重复到结果足够继续前进. 继续前进是一个生产呼吁,它平衡了创造性目标与时间和预算。 在紧凑的日程安排下,机组人员经常继续并依靠后出产来抢救未解决的缺陷(P3,P5). 基因再射会扩展出生产后可以修复的,用它,一个船员可能愿意留下的无被俘. 然而,模型实际需要发明的是什么,在设定被击中之前,仍然未知,现在捕捉更多还为时过早。 预告会直接把检查带入生产圈,在呼叫继续前.

blocks.en: On set, this visibility relieved the pressure of single-take perfection. In conventional filming, any physical departure from the planned trajectory or timing risks ruining the take. When filmmakers can inspect how departures map onto model support, single-take perfection gives way to capturing coverage. Operators can focus on capturing the live performance, knowing that secondary angles or background surfaces can be supplemented through quick pickups (P1, P2, P3). Rather than surrendering creative control to an automated model, filmmakers use diagnostic feedback to decide where physical capture is necessary and where synthetic infill is acceptable. Comfort grew because filmmakers retained active agency over what the model received, rather than relying on blind trust in generative tools (P5, P6).
blocks.zh: 设定时,这种能见度缓解了单取完美的压力. 在常规拍摄中,任何实际偏离计划轨迹或计时都有可能破坏拍摄. 当电影制片人可以检查 如何从地图到模型支持, 单摄完美让位给捕捉覆盖。 接线员可以专注于捕获活性能,知道次级角度或背景表面可以通过快取来补充(P1,P2,P3). 电影制作人不是将创意控制交给自动化模型,而是使用诊断反馈来决定物理捕捉在哪里是必要的,在哪些情况下合成填充是可以接受的. 舒适感的增长是因为电影制作人保留了该模型获得的活性代理,而不是依赖盲目地信任基因工具(P5,P6).

blocks.en: We note that not every shot warrants this workflow. For routine setups, traditional in-camera filming and quick retakes remain the fastest approach. Our workflow instead targets complex or physically constrained moves where repeated takes are costly. On set, this is only feasible because the proxy decouples interactive decision-making from generative computation. Running a full video diffusion model live would introduce latency and compute demands that immediately stall an active crew. Instead, evaluating physical coverage in milliseconds on device provides just enough structural feedback for crews to decide whether to revise the move, capture more, or accept synthesis. This architectural separation suggests a broader pattern for creative tools that integrate large generative models, such as 3D environment design, virtual production, and animation. In settings where creators rely on rapid, interactive iteration, providing fast structural proxies allows immediate steering without forcing users to wait on slow model inference.
blocks.zh: 我们注意到,并非每个机会都有理由采用这一工作流程。 对于常规设置,传统的相机拍摄和快速重拍仍然是最快的方法. 相反,我们的工作流程针对的是复杂或受到实际限制的动作,而反复采取这些动作的代价高昂。 就设定而言,这之所以可行,只是因为代理将交互决策与基因计算脱钩。 运行一个完整的视频传播模型 将引入耐性 和计算要求 立即拖住活跃的机组人员。 相反,在设备上以毫秒进行物理覆盖的评价,只是为船员提供了足够的结构反馈,可以决定是否修改移动,捕获更多,或者接受合成. 这种建筑分离为融合了3D环境设计,虚拟制作,动画等大型基因模型的创作工具提出了更广阔的模式. 在创作者依赖快速,交互式迭代的设置中,提供快速的结构代号允许即时向导而无需强迫用户等待慢模型推论.

blocks.en: 7.2. Tension Between Hallucination Risk and Creative Intent
blocks.zh: 7.2. 幻觉风险与创造性意图之间的紧张关系

blocks.en: Generative reshooting spans a spectrum between the challenges of cinematography on one end, and the risks of hallucination on the other. Decoupling camera path from camera timing gives filmmakers a clean way to plan moves along this spectrum, walking the spatial path first and sculpting its rhythm separately. It also enables automated optimization for dynamic subjects (Section 5.3 , Appendix D ). While static background geometry can always be supplemented with later pickups, a live performance happens only once. Because creators cannot film extra takes to patch a fleeting performance, our space-time search finds schedules that synchronize the authored path with the take, holding when the performer was recorded and hurrying through unobserved angles. Yet camera timing also shapes dramatic pacing and emotional tension, which an automated schedule can easily disrupt. In our study, participants valued having the search surface well-supported timing options, but preferred to sweep the slider and adjust keyframes themselves to protect their dramatic intent (DG5).
blocks.zh: 基因再拍摄横跨一端的影视挑战与另一端的幻觉风险之间. 将相机路径从相机计时中解开,让电影制作人有一条干净的方法来计划沿着这个光谱移动,先行走空间路径,并分别雕刻出它的节奏. 它还能够自动优化动态主题(第5.3节,附录D)。 虽然静态背景几何总是可以被后期的接车所补充,但现场表演只发生一次. 因为创作者不能额外拍摄补丁一瞬间性能,所以我们的时空搜索会找到将作者路径与摄取同步的时间表,在表演者被录制时会持住,并会从未观察的角度匆匆地进行. 然而相机时间也塑造出戏剧性的时间节奏和情绪紧张,而自动时间表很容易被打乱. 在我们的研究中,与会者珍视搜索表面得到良好支持的计时选项,但宁可扫荡滑盘并自行调整键框以保护其戏剧意图(DG5)。

blocks.en: Filmmakers navigated this tension directly through the compromise slider. Rather than forcing a binary choice between the recorded take and an ungrounded hallucination, the slider lets creators explore a continuous design space. In post-production, where reshooting is impossible (Part 1), participants used the slider to find a balance where a camera move gained cinematic sweep while “the footage still held” (P2). This turned camera selection into an authored trade-off between visual ambition and model support. On set (Part 2), seeing this trade-off in real time changed how participants approached capture. When the previs revealed that an ambitious target move required unseen background coverage, filmmakers did not have to pull the move back to the recorded take. Instead, guided pickups gave them a third option: capturing targeted physical evidence to support the full move they envisioned (DG2, DG4).
blocks.zh: 制片人通过折中滑板直接导航了这种张力. 滑行器不是强制在所录取和无根据幻觉之间进行二进制选择,而是让创造者探索一个连续的设计空间. 在后期制作中,如果无法重拍(第1部分),与会者利用滑动器找到一个平衡点,即相机动作在“仍然持有的镜头”的同时获得影视扫描(P2)。 这把相机选择变成了视觉野心和模型支持的作者取舍. 在设定(第2部分)时,看到这种实时取舍改变了参与者如何接近捕获. 当预告显示一个雄心勃勃的目标动作需要隐蔽的背景报道时,电影制作人不必将动作拉回所记录的拍摄. 相反,有指引的皮卡给了他们第三种选择:收集有针对性的物证以支持他们设想的全部行动(DG2,DG4)。

blocks.en: This dynamic suggests a transferable design strategy for creative human-AI tools, from generative CAD and animation to synthesized audio. When interactive systems frame AI as an all-or-nothing handoff, users often feel their authorial intent is compromised. By factorizing user intent into separable components, such as isolating spatial path from temporal rhythm, and providing continuous controls between raw input and generative completion, tools can support collaborative steering. Practitioners can then author the expressive core of a work themselves while delegating routine infill to the model.
blocks.zh: 这个动态为创造性的人类-AI工具提出了可转移的设计策略,从基因CAD和动画到合成音频. 当交互式系统将AI设定为全或一无所有交接时,用户往往感到其授权意图被破坏. 通过将用户意图纳入可分离的组件,如将空间路径从时间节奏中分离出来,并提供原始输入和基因完成之间的连续控制,工具可以支持协作引导. 然后从业者可以自己撰写作品的表达核心,同时将例行的填充权交给模型.

blocks.en: 7.3. Tension Between Plausibility and Authenticity
blocks.zh: 7.3. 透明度与真实性之间的紧张关系

blocks.en: Future improvements in generative models will reduce visual glitches and generation times. Even with higher visual fidelity, the risk of hallucination remains. Photorealistic pixels simply make inventions harder to detect. An advanced model can generate convincing facial expressions and background geometry that appear natural while bearing no relation to the physical scene. This exposes the tension between plausibility and authenticity: balancing visual enhancement against the risk of fabricating details that were never recorded. While filmmakers may accept generative synthesis for secondary background elements, our participants drew a firm line at human performance. For cinematographers, capturing a scene is the joy of the craft, not a passive handoff to post-production. Cinematographers cautioned against generative delegation that displaces the operator’s role on set (P5), emphasizing that reshooting must remain “faithful to the footage that I shot” (P4). For both practitioners, an authentic take captures deliberate choices made on set that a generative model should not rewrite.
blocks.zh: 未来基因模型的改进会减少视觉缺陷和生成时间. 即使视觉忠贞程度更高,幻觉的风险依然存在. 光现实主义像素只是使发明更难被检测. 高级模型可以产生令人信服的面部表情和背景几何,这些表情看起来自然而然,而与物理场景没有任何关系. 这暴露出可信度和真实性之间的矛盾:平衡视觉增强与编造从未被记录的细节的风险. 虽然电影制作人可能接受次生背景元素的基因合成,但我们的参与者在人类的表演上画出坚定的一行. 对于影视演员来说,捕捉一幕是工艺品的快活,而不是被动地向后出品. 电影制片人警告说,不要让传承代表团取代运营商在电视机上的角色(P5),强调重拍必须 " 忠实于我拍摄的镜头 " (P4)。 对这两位从业者来说,一个真实的录相捕捉到在设定上作出的有意的选择,即基因模型不应被改写.

blocks.en: Previsualizing hallucination risk establishes a clear boundary of visual responsibility. Showing captured evidence clarifies where a model reconstructs recorded reality and where it invents new content. In our study, participants readily allowed generative infill on textureless background walls, while strictly protecting human faces, emotional expressions, and story-critical props. This selective delegation offers a model for other domains where visual authenticity is critical, such as cultural heritage preservation, scientific visualization, and forensic documentation. In these settings, photorealistic outputs can easily mask synthetic inventions as recorded facts. Visualizing where a model lacks evidentiary support enables domain experts to selectively delegate routine synthesis while protecting the integrity of what was recorded.
blocks.zh: 幻觉风险的可视化确定了视觉责任的明确界限. 展示所获取的证据可以澄清一个模型重建记录现实的地方以及它发明出新内容的地方. 在我们的研究中,参与者很容易允许在无纹理背景墙上进行基因填充,同时严格保护人相貌,情感表达和故事关键道具. 这一选择性代表团为视觉真实性至关重要的其他领域提供了一个模式,如文化遗产保护、科学可视化和法医文献。 在这些环境下,光现实主义输出可以很容易地将合成发明掩盖为被记录的事实. 在模型缺乏证据支持的情况下可视化,使域专家能够有选择地委托例行合成,同时保护所记录内容的完整性。

blocks.en: 7.4. Limitations and Future Work
blocks.zh: 7.4. 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en: Bounded by current model capabilities: Capture and previsualization run entirely on the mobile device, while final generation occurs offline in post-production. The rendered result is therefore bounded by downstream model constraints. Current video models generate only a few seconds per call due to GPU memory limits, and slow render speeds require creators to iterate on the lightweight proxy. Splitting longer trajectories into chunks creates visual discontinuities at boundaries because current architectures do not share attention across separate generative passes. While our pipeline bridges these seams by regenerating short transitional clips (Appendix C ), doing so requires additional post-processing time.
blocks.zh: 以目前的模型能力为基础: 捕捉和预视完全运行在移动设备上,而最后一代则在后出品时被下线. 因此,所产生的结果受到下游模式的限制。 目前的视频模型由于GPU内存的限制,每通呼叫只产生几秒,而缓慢渲染速度需要创建者在轻量级代用上去除. 将较长的轨迹分割成块,在边界上产生视觉上的不连续,因为目前的架构不会在单独的基因传入中分享注意力. 虽然我们的管道通过再生短短的过渡短片(附录C)来连接这些接缝,但这样做需要更多的处理后时间。

blocks.en: Preview quality and model uncertainty: The previs visualizes physical support rather than final render appearance. Like editing proxies that enable fast playback before 4K conforming, our point cloud decouples interactive review from slow generative renders. Because point-cloud conditioning is standard across recent reshooting architectures ( Lin et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ; Cao et al., 2026 ) , our diagnostic pipeline functions as a model-agnostic, plug-and-play front end. This physical coverage provides a conservative bound for what unobserved angles must hallucinate, but models differ in how effectively they borrow distant frames or synthesize texture. Future work could train lightweight networks to translate our geometric signals into model-specific uncertainty estimates without running heavy diffusion passes on set.
blocks.zh: 预览质量和模型不确定性 : 预想中可视化物理支持而非最终使出场. 就像编辑代理在4K符合前可以快速回放, 我们的点云脱钩交互评论从慢基因产生。 因为点-云调节是跨近代重拍建筑的标准(Lin等,2026;张等,2025;Cao等,2026),我们的诊断管功能是模型-可知性,插头-并游戏前端. 这种物理覆盖为无法观察的角度必须产生幻觉提供了保守的束缚,但模型在如何有效借用远方框架或合成纹理方面有所不同. 今后的工作可以训练轻量级网络,将我们的几何信号转换成具体模型的不确定性估计,而不会在设定时进行大量扩散。

blocks.en: Camera form factors and on-device compute: Live tracking, 3D reconstruction, performer segmentation, and diagnostic evaluation all execute on a single mobile device. While mobile devices provide a convenient all-in-one platform for on-set demonstration, extended sessions cause thermal throttling that degrades processing performance, affecting video segmentation first. Furthermore, professional productions rely on specialized camera packages and external monitoring ecosystems. Future work could decouple these roles across different camera types, pairing handheld mobile directors’ monitors with cinema camera rigs or drones, while optimizing on-device pipelines to maintain interactive frame rates under sustained production use.
blocks.zh: 相机成形因子和相机上的计算 : 现场跟踪,3D重建,表演者分出,诊断评价都在一个单一的移动设备上执行. 虽然移动设备为设置上演示提供了方便的全能平台,但扩展会话导致热阻滞会降低处理性能,首先会影响视频分解. 此外,专业生产依赖于专门的相机包和外部监测生态系统。 未来的工作可以把这些角色从不同的相机类型中脱钩,将手持移动导演的显示器与电影相机平台或无人机配对,同时优化安装的管道,以便在持续生产使用的情况下保持交互式帧率。

blocks.en: 8. Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8. 结论

blocks.en: We have presented Hybrid Cinematography, a workflow that lets filmmakers see what a generative reshoot would have to hallucinate before anything is generated, and decide on set whether to revise the move, retime, capture more, or accept synthesis. Our key contribution is the previs of hallucination risk, rendered from the same proxy the model consumes, which makes that decision cheap enough to revisit after every edit and available wherever a take can be reconstructed. In our study, experienced filmmakers grew more comfortable with generative reshooting once they could evaluate hallucination risk on set and retain active control over what the model receives. Navigating the spectrum between the physical challenges of cinematography and the risks of hallucination will define the future of the craft. We expect shared representations like this proxy, which creators can visually steer and generative models can consume as conditioning, to become essential as practitioners navigate that spectrum in production.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了“混合电影摄影法 ” 这个工作流程让电影制作人看到 如何在产生任何东西之前 进行基因再拍摄, 并决定是修改动作, 重回时间, 捕捉更多, 还是接受合成。 我们的主要贡献是幻觉风险的预想,它来自模型所消耗的同一代名词,这使得这个决定在每次编辑后,只要可以重建,就足够廉价,可以重新审视。 在我们的研究中,经验丰富的电影制作人一旦能够评估幻觉风险,并保持对模型所得的主动控制,就会对基因重拍更加自在. 浏览影视的物理挑战与幻觉风险之间的频谱,将决定该工艺的未来. 我们期望这样的共同表述,即创造者能够视向引导和基因模型作为条件消耗的这种代理,在实践者在生产过程中浏览这种谱系时变得至关重要。

blocks.en: Appendix B Path Representation
blocks.zh: 附录B

blocks.en: The path must pass through every keyframe the filmmaker placed, since each one is a framing they stood in and approved, and it must be smooth enough that following it produces no jerky guidance. We therefore interpolate rather than approximate, and choose splines that are continuous in velocity. Position uses a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline ( Yuksel et al., 2011 ) , which passes through every keyframe and, unlike the uniform variant, does not overshoot or loop when two keyframes are close together. The first and last segments need a tangent from a neighbor that does not exist, so we reflect the adjacent keyframe across each end to supply one. Orientation is interpolated separately, because rotations do not live in the same space as positions and averaging them directly produces wobble; we use squad ( Shoemake, 1987 ) , the spherical counterpart of Catmull-Rom, which turns the camera smoothly through each keyframe’s orientation with tangents adjusted for uneven keyframe spacing. A shot-type preset adds interior keyframes to this same fit about a pivot chosen when it is declared (a tapped point, else the subject, else the viewfinder raycast), so a preset and a free stretch are the same kind of thing to the path. Progress along the path only increases with output time, so a retiming can hold or slow the camera but never send it backward.
blocks.zh: 道路必须穿过电影制片人所设置的每一个关键框架,因为每个框架都是他们站立和批准的框架,而且它必须足够平滑,这样它不会产生任何粗糙的指导。 因此,我们进行相插而不是相近,并选择以速度连续的分线。 位置使用一分点Catmull-Rom speline(Yuksel等,2011年),它通过每个键框,与统一变体不同,在两个键框相近时不会过度射击或循环. 第一段和最后一段需要来自一个不存在的邻居的切入剂,所以我们反映每个端相邻的键框来提供一段. 取向是分别插入的,因为取向与位置不在同一空间并直接产生摇动;我们使用小分队(Shoemake,1987年),即Catmull-Rom的球面对应方,通过每个键框的取向使相机平稳地转动,并按不均匀的键框间距调整正切. 相片型预设将内部密钥框添加到这个相片中,与宣布时所选择的枢轴(一个被调取的点,否则是主体,否则是取景者射线广播)相类似,所以预设和自由拉伸是路径的同一种. 沿着路径的进展只会随着输出时间而增加,因此回推可以把相机握住或拖慢,但永远不能向后发送.

blocks.en: Appendix C Bridging Chunk Seams
blocks.zh: 附录C 块状接合

blocks.en: We use Vista4D ( Lin et al., 2026 ) as the downstream model because it was the most recent reshooting model with open weights at the time and conditions on exactly what the workflow exports, the source video and a point cloud rendered from the target camera. It generates 49 frames per call, so a 192-frame move is generated as four chunks, and because each chunk fills in the unobserved scene differently, each join shows as a jump cut. We generate one more clip of native length centered on the join, held to the existing video at both ends and free in the middle, so the join falls inside a single generation. The ends are held by nudging the clip toward the existing video at every step, strongly at the edges and not at all near the join, in the manner of RePaint-style inpainting. The result replaces the frames around the join directly, with no blending, no training, and one extra generation per join.
blocks.zh: 我们使用Vista4D(Lin等,2026年)作为下游的模型,因为它是最新的重拍模型,在当时和条件上都以开放的重量来显示工作流程输出的准确性,源视频和从目标相机得到的点云. 它每个呼叫产生49个帧,因此192个帧的移动被生成为4个块,而由于每个块不同地填入了未观测到的场景,因此每个相接的节目作为跳跃切. 我们再制作一集以加盟为中心的本土长度的片段,在两端分别被保存在现有的视频上,中间是免费的,因此加盟落在一代人之内. 以RePaint风格的绘画方式, 结果直接取代了加盟周围的帧,没有混合,没有训练,每加盟增加一代.

blocks.en:
Because timing is authored separately (Section 5.1 ), the
system can search over it. The Retime proposal treats retiming as
synchronizing the authored path with the recorded take. On a grid of path
progress against take time, a schedule is a curve that only moves forward
in both, a hold is a horizontal run, and each cell costs by how far the
authored camera is from where the real camera was at that instant, how
under-resolved the room is from there, and how much of the performer that
view fails to see. Dynamic programming returns the cheapest schedule, with
holds and hand-authored spans frozen so a search cannot undo a deliberate
decision. The search may also stop short of the path’s end, and a combined
search finds the least shortening that leaves the performer supported
throughout. Either result is shown as a proposal with its consequences and
applied only if the filmmaker accepts it (DG5), and nothing is offered when
any instant would remain unsupported or unknown.

This appendix documents the study responses summarized in
Section 6 . Part 1 comprised an introductory sequence and a
second scene in an interactive browser viewer. In Part 2, participants used

blocks.en: E.1. Part 1 Tasks and Scoring
blocks.zh: E.1. 第1部分 任务和计分

blocks.en:
The initial pin task paired the source take with a generated image at frame
42. Participants were told that the source camera had filmed the actor from
the side and asked to click content the camera had never seen. The reveal
showed the reference mask and a separately annotated face region. A coverage
lesson then compared the reconstructed proxy with a generated result, followed
by a slider demonstration. This was an instructed exercise, not an unaided
test of detecting generated content.
blocks.zh:

blocks.en:
The second scene used the orbit target at frame 86 in the recorded sessions.
Participants first pinned missing content in the proxy with overlays hidden,
then viewed coverage and performer warnings, chose a slider stop, completed
two checks, and explored the viewer while answering closing questions. The
resolution overlay was disabled. The checks assessed interpretation of the performer
heat scale and comparison of generation needs between two camera stops.

Participants explained their chosen stop with a prompt suggesting
actor-face versus background-room tradeoffs. Closing items
asked about comfort with generative video reshooting,
preferred preview timing (on set, editing, both, or neither), reasons for those
answers, and one desired change. P1 and P4 asked to edit the camera path directly, P2 wanted a limit on
viewpoint departure, P3 asked for a preview of a paused frame, P5 for a
preview of the generated options, P6 for an automatic pan that surveys
the scene while shooting, and P7 for integration with editing software such
as Adobe Premiere. These requests are individual suggestions, not
shared themes.

blocks.en: E.2. Part 2 Ratings
blocks.zh: E.2. 第2部分 评级

blocks.en:
The Part 2 questionnaire asked participants to reflect on their use of the
mobile AR application. Questions covered planning, guidance, review, and future workflow
integration in that order. The questionnaire included interface illustrations
and examples of moves difficult or expensive to execute physically, such as
robotic camera movement and dolly crews. Table 2 summarizes all Part 2 ratings. Agreement items used 1 (strongly disagree), 4 (neutral),
and 7 (strongly agree). The comfort item used 1 (not at all comfortable) and
7 (completely comfortable). Item numbers in the table match the questionnaire.

blocks.en:
The storytelling question additionally suggested actors, key props, faces, and
emotions versus background geometry, ceilings, and distant walls. The guidance
and review questions also described expected benefits. Accordingly, the
responses should be read in the context of these examples and framings.
